decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY captures aggregate counts but omits the explicit rule that every accounted ticket must have a corresponding $5 commission.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
So far, we have done 12 mints, that should equal 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**When there is no referral code used, there is still a ticket and commission**.

Right now, **when a code is used**, it is correctly accounted for on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

When there is **no referral code used**, the ticket and commission are randomly assigned.
(B**ut they still need to be accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I think since your last fix, (on the last 2 mints) the randomly assigned tickets have been accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
But they have not been backfilled to show the missing tickets.

And the commissions (from these no code buys) are still not being accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot you'll see i have an NFT with 2 tickets and only 1 x $5 commission - this should be impossible, as every ticket comes with a $5 commission.

And on my leaderboard screenshot, you can count (from 12 total mints) 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions accounted for.
12 mints should equal 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions, regardless of a referral code being used or not.

value_updates.expected_aggregate_rule: Each mint must be represented by one ticket and one $5 commission in reward-accounting views, whether a referral code is used or the reward is randomly assigned.
value_updates.ticket_commission_pairing_rule: Every accounted ticket must have a corresponding $5 commission in reward-accounting views.

decisions.reason: The source addresses runtime accounting in leaderboards and NFT attributes, not a required change to FAQ copy.
Ticket and commission accounting does not change badge definitions, milestones, storage, or award behavior.
Reward metadata accounting is independent of NFT image, ebook-link, and wallet asset rendering.
The source does not affect the responsive arrangement of badges.
The source changes accounting visibility, not fiat-wallet provisioning, authentication, reward access, or cash-out guidance.
The About-page state already describes random no-code rewards, and the source does not request a copy change.

The candidate already requires one randomly assigned $5 commission and Small Block ticket per no-referral primary mint; the source reports their missing accounting rather than changing allocation behavior.
The source does not direct any change to Mission-page messaging.
The candidate already requires one ticket per successful primary mint, including no-referral mints; the source concerns display and accounting rather than ticket issuance, eligibility, or expiration.
The accounting clarification does not change landing-page hero copy or layout.
The source concerns primary-mint ticket and commission accounting and does not change secondary-sale royalties or marketplace enforcement.
